intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Spend an afternoon and evening immersed in the heart of Marrakech's UNESCO-listed medina. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians perform in the square, then wander through the historic souks buying spices, leather goods, and lanterns. With a late Day 1 arrival, skip this on arrival night and begin fresh on Day 2 morning when crowds are manageable and light is ideal for photography. Stay within walking distance by booking a riad inside the medina walls.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Overnight Camp at Erg Chebbi
experiences.description: Journey to the iconic golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a 2-night desert experience. Ride camels at sunset into a traditional Berber camp, enjoy a tagine dinner under a sky full of stars, and wake at dawn for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes. This is the cultural and natural highlight of any Marrakech-Sahara itinerary and worth allocating Days 3–5 to allow travel time and full immersion. Book a camp within the dunes themselves to minimize transfer time.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Explore two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks back to back, both located within the southern medina. The 19th-century Bahia Palace dazzles with intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedar ceilings, while the Saadian Tombs offer a rare glimpse into the royal burial chambers of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty. Combine both in a half-day morning visit to beat the heat and crowds. Staying in a medina riad puts you within a 10-minute walk of both sites.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class with Market Visit
experiences.description: Join a small-group cooking class led by a local chef, beginning with a guided tour of the Mellah spice market to select fresh ingredients. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as chicken bastilla, harira soup, and orange-blossom couscous. Classes typically run 4 hours and include a full sit-down meal. Choose a school located inside or adjacent to the medina to avoid long transfers, especially useful for Days 2 or 6 when you are based in Marrakech.

experiences.name: Aït Benhaddou Kasbah & Draa Valley Day Trip
experiences.description: En route to or from the Sahara on Days 3 or 5, stop at the UNESCO World Heritage ksar of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning fortified mud-brick village used as a backdrop for films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, Morocco's longest river valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, palm groves, and Berber villages. This route is a natural stop on the Marrakech-to-Merzouga road, eliminating any detour and maximizing your travel days efficiently.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or negotiate a petit taxi (aim for 70–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings. The Medina at night has a magical, lantern-lit atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on the plane
meals.lunch: N/A – on the plane
meals.dinner: If hungry after arrival, grab a late-night snack from a street cart near Jemaa el-Fna square (open until midnight+). Try a bowl of harira soup (5–10 MAD) or msemen flatbread (3–5 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Keep some small dirham bills handy for the taxi. Exchange currency at the airport or use an ATM (Wafa Bank or CIH Bank have fair rates). Hotel Aday is a budget riad-style guesthouse – confirm your late check-in with them in advance. Rest well; big day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at a local café near the hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou (almond-argan dip), and hard-boiled eggs for around 20–30 MAD. Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5 min walk) and explore the surrounding souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market), and Souk Cherratin (leather). Bargain confidently – first prices are always inflated. Budget 2–3 hours for souk exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue (free or small donation). Stop by the Mellah market for fresh olives, preserved lemons, and local snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at sunset to witness the square transform into a massive open-air carnival – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls. Eat dinner at the communal food stalls (stalls 1–100 area) – try grilled merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget around 50–80 MAD for a full meal.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel – mint tea, msemen, amlou – ~25 MAD
meals.lunch: Snack in the souks – bissara (fava bean soup) and bread at a hole-in-the-wall stall near Souk des Épices – ~15–20 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled meats, salads, harira, fresh OJ – ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Keep your bag in front of you in crowded souks. Avoid accepting 'free' henna or unsolicited guide services. The Bahia Palace opens at 9:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims – free) to see the iconic 12th-century minaret at its most photogenic in the morning light. Then head to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century with intricate stucco and zellige tilework. Arrive early (opens 9 AM) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the walls. Afterward, visit the Museum of Marrakech (Musée de Marrakech) housed in a gorgeous 19th-century mansion (~50 MAD) for Moroccan art, ceramics, and photography exhibits. Take a rest break at a rooftop café overlooking the Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Mouassine neighborhood for a quieter, more authentic evening. Visit the Mouassine Fountain and explore the artisan workshops. Have dinner at a local restaurant on Rue Mouassine – try a traditional tagine (chicken with preserved lemon or lamb with prunes) for 50–80 MAD. End the evening with a walk back through the lit-up Medina alleys.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a nearby café – café au lait and khobz bread with olive oil – ~20 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant near El Badi Palace – vegetable couscous or lentil soup with bread – ~40–50 MAD
meals.dinner: Rue Mouassine local restaurant – lamb or chicken tagine with bread – ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Saadian Tombs can get crowded by 10 AM – arrive right at opening. El Badi Palace has a rooftop terrace with panoramic views – worth the climb. Budget total for entrance fees today: ~190 MAD. Carry water; March can be warm in the afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley (about 30 km from Marrakech). Take a shared grand taxi from Bab Rob taxi stand (~30–40 MAD per person each way) to the valley. Hike along the Ourika River through Berber villages, terraced gardens, and almond/olive groves. Visit a local Berber family home for mint tea (often offered freely or for a small tip). The scenery is lush and the Atlas Mountains backdrop is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley to the Setti Fatma waterfalls (about 1 hour hike from the road – wear sturdy shoes). The lower falls are accessible and rewarding. Have lunch at one of the riverside terrace restaurants in Setti Fatma village – fresh trout from the river is a local specialty (~60–80 MAD for a full meal). Head back to Marrakech by shared taxi in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at the hotel after the day trip. For dinner, explore the Bab Doukkala neighborhood near the Medina for a truly local experience – no tourists, just neighborhood restaurants serving home-style Moroccan food. Try a rotisserie chicken (half chicken + bread + salad for ~40–50 MAD) or a bowl of trid (shredded pastry with chicken and lentils).

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before departure – café near Bab Rob – msemen and tea – ~20 MAD
meals.lunch: Riverside restaurant in Setti Fatma – fresh trout or tagine with salad and bread – ~70 MAD
meals.dinner: Bab Doukkala neighborhood local restaurant – rotisserie chicken or trid – ~45 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (8:00–8:30 AM) to maximize time in the valley. Shared grand taxis fill up quickly – be patient at the stand. Bring a light jacket as the valley can be cooler than Marrakech. The hike to the waterfalls involves some scrambling over rocks – take care. Total transport cost for the day: ~80 MAD.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a shared/group budget transfer or CTM bus toward Ouarzazate and Merzouga. The most budget-friendly option is a shared minibus or organized budget group tour (book in advance for ~350–500 MAD per person for a 2-day/1-night Sahara trip including transport, camel ride, and desert camp). The route crosses the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas – breathtaking scenery. Stop at Aït Benhaddou UNESCO World Heritage ksar (ancient fortified village) for a 1–2 hour visit (~10 MAD entrance).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Draa Valley and Dadès Gorge region, passing kasbahs, palm oases, and rose fields (March is near rose season). Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dune area by late afternoon. Check into a budget desert camp or guesthouse on the edge of the dunes (~150–200 MAD per person for a basic camp with dinner and breakfast included).
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes – one of the most iconic experiences in Morocco. Watch the sun set over the golden sand sea. Spend the night at a desert camp under a sky full of stars – no light pollution means extraordinary stargazing. Enjoy a communal dinner of tagine and couscous around a campfire with Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure or packed snacks – ~20 MAD
meals.lunch: Roadside stop near Ouarzazate or Aït Benhaddou – sandwich or tagine at a local café – ~40–50 MAD
meals.dinner: Included at desert camp – traditional tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, mint tea – included in camp fee

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour/transfer at least 2–3 days in advance from Marrakech – many budget hostels and riads can arrange this. The drive is long (8–10 hours total) but the scenery is spectacular. Bring a scarf/shemagh for the camel ride (sand can blow). Temperatures drop significantly at night in the desert – bring a warm layer even in March. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the nearest dune and watch the sunrise over the Sahara – an unforgettable, life-changing moment. The colors shift from deep purple to orange to gold. Take your time photographing and simply absorbing the silence of the desert. Return to camp for a simple breakfast (included). Explore the base of the dunes on foot and visit the small village of Merzouga for a walk through the local market and a visit to a nomadic family if arranged through your camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey to Marrakech (or continue to Fes if extending the trip). On the return, consider stopping at the Todra Gorge (dramatic 300m-high canyon walls) if your transport route allows – a short walk through the gorge is free and stunning. Stop for lunch in Ouarzazate – the 'Hollywood of Morocco' known for its film studios (Atlas Studios exterior is free to view). Arrive back in Marrakech by late evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech tired but exhilarated. Freshen up at Hotel Aday. For a low-key evening, grab street food near the hotel – a kefta sandwich from a grill stall (~15–20 MAD) or a bowl of harira with chebakia pastry (~10 MAD). Early night to recover.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp – bread, jam, eggs, mint tea
meals.lunch: Ouarzazate local restaurant – chicken tagine or sandwich – ~40–50 MAD
meals.dinner: Street food near Hotel Aday – kefta sandwich or harira – ~20–30 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is equally scenic but you'll be tired – try to sleep in the vehicle. If your budget tour includes a second night in the desert, this is worth considering for deeper exploration. Keep your camera accessible for the sunrise – it's the highlight of the entire trip for most travelers. Drink plenty of water; desert air is very dry.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD – splurge-worthy) or the free alternative: the Agdal Gardens (free, a vast royal orchard south of the Medina, open on Fridays and Sundays). The Agdal is a hidden gem with olive, orange, and pomegranate trees and a large reflecting pool – very peaceful and authentically local. Enjoy a slow final breakfast at a rooftop café with Medina views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last souk shopping for souvenirs – best budget buys include: argan oil (buy from a women's cooperative for fair prices), leather goods in Souk Cherratin, hand-painted ceramics, and Berber spices. Head to the Ensemble Artisanal (government-fixed prices, no bargaining needed – good reference for fair prices). Pack your bags and check out of Hotel Aday. Store luggage at the hotel if your flight is late.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner at a beloved local institution – try Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima for a rooftop farewell meal (tagine ~80–100 MAD) or the ultra-budget option of one last round at the Jemaa el-Fna food stalls. Reflect on the week's adventures over a final glass of fresh-squeezed orange juice (5 MAD – the best value in Morocco). Head to the airport – allow 45–60 minutes from the Medina.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop café near the Medina – full Moroccan breakfast spread – ~40–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Light lunch – msemen with honey and argan oil at a café – ~25 MAD
meals.dinner: Café des Épices or Jemaa el-Fna stalls – tagine or grilled meats – ~80–100 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Agdal Gardens are only open to the public on Fridays and Sundays – perfect timing for Day 7 (Sunday). If Majorelle Garden is on your must-do list, budget the 150 MAD entrance (includes the Berber Museum). Tip your hotel staff before checkout – 20–30 MAD is appreciated. Keep 200–300 MAD in cash for the airport taxi. Total estimated 7-day budget (excluding flights and accommodation): 1,500–2,200 MAD (~$150–220 USD) per person.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30. Check in to Hotel Aday in the Medina, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport taxi or ride-share (~150–200 MAD) to Hotel Aday in Derb Sidi Bouloukat. Check in, unwind with mint tea if offered by the riad, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: If hungry upon arrival, grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store in the Medina, or ask the hotel if a late snack is available.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival logistics simple. Confirm your taxi or transfer in advance. The Medina's narrow alleys can be tricky at night — ask the hotel to send GPS coordinates or meet you at a nearby landmark like Jemaa el-Fna square.

day_by_day.morning: After a restful sleep, enjoy breakfast at the hotel. Then walk to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (5-minute walk) to soak in the morning atmosphere — orange juice vendors, locals heading to work, and the buzz of the Medina waking up. Head into the souks (Souk Semmarine, Souk des Épices) for a 2-hour self-guided exploration of spices, leather goods, ceramics, and textiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (15-minute walk from the hotel, ~70 MAD entry) — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and lush gardens. Afterward, explore the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the Saadian Tombs (~70 MAD entry), a beautifully preserved royal necropolis from the 16th century.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk to witness the square transform into a vibrant open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Stroll the perimeter and take it all in before dinner.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday — most riads include a traditional Moroccan breakfast (msemen flatbread, honey, argan oil, olives, mint tea).
meals.lunch: Café des Épices near Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace with great views, tagines and salads for ~80–120 MAD per person.
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls — try harira soup, merguez sausages, and kefta skewers for an authentic and affordable experience (~60–100 MAD). Alternatively, Restaurant Chez Lamine for slow-cooked mechoui lamb (~150 MAD).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are cobblestone and uneven. Bargaining is expected in the souks; start at 40–50% of the asking price. Keep a small amount of cash (MAD) handy for entry fees and food stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior only for non-Muslims) and the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD entry) — a 16th-century palace with sweeping views from the ramparts and resident storks nesting on the walls. Then head to the Maison de la Photographie or the Museum of Moroccan Arts (Dar Si Said, ~30 MAD) for cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short taxi to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (~150 MAD combined entry) — a vivid cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, now one of Marrakech's most photographed spots. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the exotic plants, Berber museum, and the adjacent YSL memorial garden.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the Medina for a relaxed evening. Explore the quieter northern souks (Souk Haddadine — the blacksmiths' souk) and browse artisan workshops. End the evening with a traditional hammam experience at a mid-range public hammam near the Medina (~150–250 MAD for a full scrub and massage).

meals.breakfast: At the hotel.
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif near the Majorelle Garden area — colorful, vegetarian-friendly café with Moroccan salads and wraps (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: Le Foundouk restaurant in the northern Medina — beautifully restored caravanserai with Moroccan-French fusion cuisine; tagines and pastilla (~200–300 MAD per person, mid-range splurge).

day_by_day.notes: Book Majorelle Garden tickets online in advance — it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience; ask the hotel to recommend a reputable local one rather than a tourist-oriented spa.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (6:00–7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — join a shared or private day-tour to the Draa Valley and Zagora, OR opt for the more popular 2-day/1-night Merzouga (Erg Chebbi) excursion. For a 7-day trip, a private overnight Merzouga tour (departing today, returning tomorrow evening) is highly recommended. The drive takes ~8–9 hours via the High Atlas Mountains and Draa Valley — scenery is spectacular. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the drive through the Atlas Mountains, passing through Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Africa') — stop briefly at the Kasbah Taourirt (~30 MAD entry), a stunning earthen fortress. Continue southeast through the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley) and the dramatic Draa Valley palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at the edge of the Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga (~18:00–19:00). Mount camels for a 45-minute sunset ride into the dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sun set over the Sahara — one of Morocco's most breathtaking experiences. Enjoy a Berber dinner under the stars with live drumming and music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks for the road.
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate or a stop along the route — traditional tagine set menu (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Included at the desert camp — traditional Berber meal: harira, tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea under the stars.

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable tour operator in advance (e.g., Sahara Expedition, Desert Majesty, or through your hotel). Mid-range overnight desert camp costs ~600–900 MAD per person including camel ride, dinner, breakfast, and a private or semi-private tent. March weather in the Sahara is ideal — warm days (~25°C), cool nights (~10°C). Bring a light jacket, sunscreen, and a headscarf for the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) for a magical Sahara sunrise over the dunes — one of the most memorable moments of the trip. Take a short walk or sandboard on the dunes. Enjoy a simple breakfast at the camp (mint tea, bread, honey, eggs). Begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Todra Gorge — a dramatic 300m-high canyon carved by the Todra River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at the Todra Gorge for a 1-hour walk through the narrow canyon (free entry). Continue west through the Dades Gorge (the 'Road of a Thousand Kasbahs') — stop at a roadside café for lunch and admire the dramatic rock formations. Continue driving back toward Marrakech through the High Atlas.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech (~19:00–20:00). Check back into Hotel Aday, shower, and decompress. Take a gentle evening stroll around Jemaa el-Fna for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Included at the desert camp.
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant in the Dades Valley — fresh salads, tagine, and fresh-squeezed juice (~80–120 MAD).
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant near Place des Épices in Marrakech — modern Moroccan cuisine on a rooftop terrace with Medina views; lamb pastilla or vegetable couscous (~180–250 MAD per person).

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (~8–9 hours with stops). Bring water, snacks, and a good playlist or podcast. The Todra Gorge is best visited in the morning light. If energy allows, a short evening walk to Jemaa el-Fna is a great way to re-immerse in city life after the desert.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient Roman ruins of Volubilis and the holy city of Moulay Idriss — OR, if you prefer to stay closer to Marrakech, take a half-day excursion to the Ourika Valley in the Atlas Mountains (45 minutes from Marrakech). The Ourika Valley offers Berber villages, a waterfall hike, and stunning mountain scenery. Visit a local argan oil cooperative run by Berber women for a free demonstration and fair-trade shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Marrakech by early afternoon. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (housed in a stunning 19th-century palace, ~50 MAD) for Moroccan art and historical artifacts. Spend the remaining afternoon doing any last-minute souk shopping — pick up saffron, argan oil, leather goods, or handwoven textiles as souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge on a special farewell dinner at a traditional Moroccan riad restaurant. Enjoy a full Moroccan feast: pastilla (pigeon or chicken pie), lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, couscous, and chebakia (honey pastry) for dessert — all served in an atmospheric candlelit courtyard.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel.
meals.lunch: In the Ourika Valley — a simple Berber lunch at a family-run mountain restaurant with panoramic views (~80–120 MAD); or a quick lunch at a Medina café upon return.
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or Riad Dar Zitoun — iconic Marrakech riad dining experience with live Gnawa music; budget ~300–400 MAD per person for a full set menu (a worthwhile splurge for the final evening).

day_by_day.notes: The Ourika Valley excursion can be done by shared taxi (grand taxi) from Bab Rob gate for ~50–80 MAD each way, or via a guided half-day tour (~300–500 MAD). Saturday is market day in some Atlas villages — a great opportunity to see local Berber commerce. Book the riad dinner in advance as popular spots fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take one last slow walk through the Medina to revisit your favorite spots: the spice souk, a rooftop café for mint tea, or the peaceful Koutoubia gardens. Visit any remaining sights you may have missed — the Almoravid Koubba (the oldest surviving monument in Marrakech, ~20 MAD) is a hidden gem near the Musée de Marrakech.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, use the afternoon for final packing, souvenir shopping, or a relaxed café stop. Check out of Hotel Aday and arrange a taxi to the airport. Marrakech Menara Airport is about 15–20 minutes from the Medina (~100–150 MAD by taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Marrakech Menara Airport. Carry memories of the Medina's labyrinthine souks, the golden Sahara dunes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at the hotel — savor the mint tea, msemen, and honey one last time.
meals.lunch: Café du Grand Balcon overlooking Jemaa el-Fna — a classic Marrakech institution with great views and simple Moroccan fare (~100–150 MAD).
meals.dinner: At the airport or on the plane.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some MAD for the taxi and any last-minute purchases. Duty-free at Marrakech airport has a decent selection of Moroccan argan products and spices if you run out of time to shop in the Medina.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina. A dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Check-in, unwind with a welcome mint tea and traditional pastries prepared by the riad.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival only. After check-in, enjoy a light in-room supper arranged by the hotel: Moroccan harira soup, msemen flatbread, and fresh fruit. Rest and acclimatize to the Medina atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (travel day)
meals.dinner: Private in-room welcome supper at Hotel Aday — harira soup, msemen, seasonal fruit, and Moroccan mint tea (arranged in advance with the hotel)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. The Medina streets are narrow; a hotel representative will meet you at the Medina gate with luggage assistance. Keep the first night light — no excursions planned.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a private guided walking tour of the Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding souks — spice market (Souk des Épices), leather tanneries viewpoint, and the dyers' souk. Your private guide will provide deep cultural and historical context. Visit the 14th-century Ben Youssef Madrasa, one of the most ornate Islamic colleges in North Africa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided tour of the Saadian Tombs — a hidden royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, featuring exquisite Andalusian tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Continue to the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century grand vizier's palace with lush gardens and intricately painted ceilings. Enjoy a private photography session in the palace's most photogenic courtyards.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop terrace of a premier Medina restaurant such as Nomad or Le Jardin, overlooking the rooftops of Marrakech. Dinner at Le Foundouk — a celebrated fine-dining restaurant in a restored 18th-century caravanserai, offering refined Moroccan cuisine: bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and orange blossom crème brûlée.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday — fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan pancakes (baghrir), honey, argan oil, olives, and eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices on Place Rahba Kedima — rooftop terrace, mezze platters, grilled kefta, and fresh lemonade
meals.dinner: Le Foundouk, Marrakech Medina — refined Moroccan fine dining with wine pairing (approx. MAD 600–900 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Ben Youssef Madrasa tickets in advance — it can be crowded mid-morning. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina cobblestones. A private licensed guide is strongly recommended for the souks to avoid tourist pressure.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). Explore the cobalt-blue villa, exotic botanical garden, and the Berber Museum within the grounds. The YSL Museum houses rotating exhibitions on fashion, art, and the designer's deep connection to Morocco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full traditional hammam and spa experience at a luxury hammam such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa (day access). Enjoy a black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, argan oil massage, and relaxation in the steam room. Return to the hotel for a rest before the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Private rooftop dinner experience at Dar Yacout — one of Marrakech's most iconic and atmospheric restaurants, set inside a stunning 1930s palace. Multi-course Moroccan feast: pastilla, couscous royale, mechoui lamb, and traditional desserts, accompanied by live Gnawa music and candlelight.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday — fresh fruit platter, msemen with honey and butter, Moroccan mint tea, and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Kif Kif near the Majorelle Garden — salads, sandwiches, and fresh juices in a relaxed garden setting
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout, Marrakech — iconic palace dining experience with live music (reservation essential; approx. MAD 700–1,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the YSL Museum and hammam well in advance — both are extremely popular. The hammam session typically lasts 2–3 hours. Dar Yacout requires a reservation; request a rooftop table for the best atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (07:00) in a private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the scenic drive to the Sahara Desert via the Draa Valley and Dades Gorge. Stop at the Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas for panoramic photos and fresh mountain air. Continue through the ancient ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and famous film location (Gladiator, Game of Thrones). Private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the journey through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) near Kelaat M'Gouna, famous for its Damask rose fields (peak bloom in April, but the valley is scenic year-round). Stop at a local cooperative to learn about rose water and argan oil production. Arrive at the luxury desert camp near Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) by late afternoon. Check in to your private luxury tent — expect en-suite bathrooms, king beds, and elegant Berber décor.
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek at golden hour into the Erg Chebbi dunes — watch the sunset paint the 150-meter-high sand dunes in shades of amber and crimson. Return to camp for a private candlelit dinner under the stars: Berber tagine, couscous, grilled meats, and traditional sweets. Live Gnawa and Berber drum music around the campfire. Optional stargazing session with a telescope provided by the camp.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure — packed travel breakfast if needed (arranged with hotel)
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a local family home near Aït Benhaddou — slow-cooked lamb tagine, fresh bread, and mint tea (arranged by your guide)
meals.dinner: Private candlelit dinner at the luxury desert camp — multi-course Moroccan feast with live Berber music

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops. An early start is essential. Ensure your private driver is licensed and experienced on mountain roads. Pack a light jacket — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Luxury desert camps to consider: Scarabeo Camp, Erg Chebbi Luxury Camp, or Merzouga Luxury Desert Camp.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise camel or quad bike ride to the top of the highest dune in Erg Chebbi. Watch the sunrise illuminate the vast Sahara in silence — one of Morocco's most extraordinary experiences. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a 4x4 desert excursion to a remote nomadic Berber family encampment for tea and conversation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Merzouga village and the Gnawa musicians' quarter — learn about the spiritual healing music tradition of the Gnawa people. Explore the fossil and mineral markets unique to this region. Begin the return journey toward the Todra Gorge (Gorges du Todra) — dramatic 300-meter-high limestone canyon walls. Short hike through the gorge with your guide. Check in to a luxury kasbah hotel in the Dades Valley for the night (e.g., Kasbah Panorama or Xaluca Dades).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Dades River with views of the rose-red kasbahs. Dinner at the kasbah hotel — traditional Moroccan spread: harira, pastilla, lamb mechoui, and seasonal vegetables, paired with Moroccan rosé wine.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the luxury desert camp — fresh fruit, Moroccan pancakes, eggs, honey, argan oil, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Tinghir near the Todra Gorge — grilled brochettes, salads, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.dinner: Dinner at the luxury kasbah hotel in the Dades Valley — traditional Moroccan multi-course dinner

day_by_day.notes: The sunrise experience in the Sahara is the highlight of the trip — do not miss it. Bring a warm layer for the pre-dawn camel ride. The drive from Merzouga to the Dades Valley is approximately 3–4 hours with stops.

day_by_day.morning: Morning exploration of the Dades Gorge — the 'Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs.' Drive through the dramatic switchback road known as the 'Monkey Fingers' rock formations. Stop at a traditional Berber village for a guided walk and mint tea with a local family. Begin the return journey to Marrakech via the Ouarzazate — the 'Hollywood of Africa.' Visit the Atlas Film Studios, the world's largest film studio, where Lawrence of Arabia, Babel, and Kingdom of Heaven were filmed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Ouarzazate's Taourirt Kasbah — a UNESCO-listed 19th-century palace complex, once home to the powerful Glaoui clan. Private guided tour with a local historian. Depart for Marrakech via the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Arrive back at Hotel Aday by early evening. Freshen up and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's finest restaurants — La Maison Arabe (a legendary institution since 1946), offering refined Moroccan haute cuisine: bastilla au fruits de mer, lamb with prunes and almonds, and traditional pastilla au lait for dessert. After dinner, a final stroll through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square — fire eaters, storytellers, and musicians create an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the kasbah hotel — fresh bread, local honey, Berber omelette, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch in Ouarzazate at Restaurant Chez Dimitri — a historic restaurant serving Moroccan and Mediterranean cuisine since 1928
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe, Marrakech — legendary fine dining with live traditional music (reservation essential; approx. MAD 700–1,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Dades to Marrakech via Ouarzazate is approximately 5–6 hours with stops. Depart the kasbah by 08:00 to allow time for all stops. La Maison Arabe also offers cooking classes — consider booking one for the morning if you return early.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century Saadian palace once described as one of the wonders of the world, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts. Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and its historic synagogues and spice merchants. Last-minute luxury shopping in the Medina: argan oil, handwoven carpets, leather goods, and Moroccan ceramics at reputable fixed-price shops recommended by your concierge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell lunch at a rooftop restaurant. Return to the hotel for final packing. Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Enjoy a final glass of fresh orange juice — Morocco's signature farewell gift.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry the memories of the Sahara stars, the call to prayer echoing through the Medina, and the scent of rose water and spices.

meals.breakfast: Final rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday — full Moroccan spread with fresh orange juice, pastries, eggs, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Nomad Restaurant, Marrakech — contemporary Moroccan cuisine with stunning Medina rooftop views (approx. MAD 300–500 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining (departure day)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the airport transfer and check-in — Marrakech Menara Airport can be busy. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange a reputable carpet or argan oil shop visit to avoid tourist traps. Consider purchasing a bottle of Moroccan rose water or a small Berber rug as a premium souvenir.
